title: delta-epoch-compact-manifest-v0
content:
Purpose:
A compact, appendable manifest format for epoch-based session deltas. The goal is a minimal wire/storage structure that supports fast resume, integrity checks, incremental verification, and low parsing overhead in the proxy/edge path. This is a personal draft — rough, opinionated, and intentionally small to iterate quickly.

Motivation / Constraints:
- Operate on unreliable networks: partial writes, truncated uploads, and replay.
- Want a manifest that can be scanned forward-only by small CPU-bound agents (edge runners) without allocating large heaps.
- Support incremental application of deltas (append-only), cheap integrity checks (fast checksums), and a clear boundary between metadata and payload.
- Compatible with existing KV-cache checkpoints, but smaller metadata footprint per-epoch.

Primary use cases:
- Session offload: evict inactive session fragments to object store and reconstruct quickly on first access.
- Cross-region transfer: ship compact epoch blobs between regions for failover.
- Debugging & audits: small manifest entries make it easier to sample and verify changes.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Human-readable header, binary-compact payload pointers.
- Append-only ledger of epoch entries with monotonically increasing epoch_index.
- Each epoch entry contains: timestamp, short provenance tag, compressed delta reference (digest + length), and resume hints.
- Fast-skip scanning: entries prefixed with 2-byte length + 4-byte checksum to skip corrupted entries.
- Backwards compatible: v0 should allow extension tags that are ignored by older parsers.

Top-level file layout (byte-level sketch):
[FILE_HEADER] -> ascii: "DELMANv0\n" (8 bytes)
[ENTRY]* (repeated)
[FOOTER_INDEX] optional for random access

ENTRY layout (serialized, tight):
- entry_len: uint16 (2 bytes) -- total length of the following entry body (allows forward-scan skip)
- entry_csum: uint32 (4 bytes) -- crc32 of the entry body (cheap detect)
- entry_body: bytes (entry_len bytes) -- TLV-like compact structure

ENTRY_BODY TLVs (order preferred but not required):
- T(0x01) epoch_index: varint (small)
- T(0x02) ts: unix_ms (varint)
- T(0x03) provenance: short ASCII (len + bytes, max 32)
- T(0x04) payload_digest: sha256 (32 bytes) OR short-fingerprint (8 bytes) if label set to fingerprint
- T(0x05) payload_len: varint
- T(0x06) resume_hint: ascii (len + bytes, e.g., "kv://key/ctx/frag-3")
- T(0x0F) ext: opaque (len + bytes) for future tags

Notes on types:
- Use varint (LEB128) for small integers to keep short entries tiny.
- Allow payload_digest to be either full sha256 (for store-level verification) or an 8-byte truncated blake/fingerprint for speed. Variant indicated by a 1-byte flavor marker in the digest TLV.

Example (conceptual, not bytes):
[entry_len=85][csum=0x9a7f1234][body: epoch=42, ts=1701..., provenance="edge-prefetch", digest_flavor=0x01, digest=sha256:..., payload_len=624, resume_hint="kv://s/abc/frag-42"]

Recovery semantics:
- Scan sequentially; for each entry, read entry_len then attempt to read entry_body. If read fails (truncated storage), stop and return last-known-good epoch.
- If entry_body read succeeds but entry_csum mismatches, skip to next candidate by advancing 1 byte and resyncing to next plausible entry_len (best-effort). Keep a small scan window for resync heuristics.
- Footer_index (optional): periodic index mapping epoch_index -> file_offset placed every N entries to permit faster seeks. Not required for correctness.

Storage and transport strategies:
- Store payloads separately in blob store keyed by payload_digest. The manifest only references payloads. Payloads themselves are content-addressed and immutable.
- When transporting between regions, send all entry bodies and any referenced payloads. Receiver can deduplicate by fingerprint.

Resumption API shape (edge runner sketch):
- GET /session/{id}/manifest?from_epoch=last_known -> stream entries starting at next epoch.
- POST /session/{id}/manifest/append -> append entries (idempotent if payload_digest already exists).
- HEAD /blob/{digest} -> check existence, size, and quick fingerprint.
(These are sketchy; exact HTTP schema TBD with gateway team.)

Rollout considerations:
- Start with v0 read-only support in edge: edges assume manifest v0 and can still read older checkpoint formats.
- Write-path toggled via feature flag. When enabled, runtime will start emitting compact-manifest entries in addition to current checkpoint blobs for 30 days before switching reads to manifest-first.

Testing checklist (quick):
- property tests: append-only invariants, monotonic epoch_index, resume returns consistent reassembly
- fuzz: truncated reads, random byte corruption, interleaved writes
- perf: parse throughput on 1 CPU core reading 10k entries/s; memory under 512KB
- integration: end-to-end offload and resume with kv-store and object-store (S3/GCS)

Open questions / tradeoffs (personal TODOs):
- digest flavor: full sha256 vs 8-byte fingerprint — how often do we need full cryptographic guarantees vs speed?
- should resume_hint be a structured mini-uri or free text? URIs allow deterministic parsing but are longer.
- index cadence for footer_index: every 64 entries or time-based (every 15s)?
- compaction: strategy for tombstoning replaced epochs and safe GC of payloads. Do we emit tombstone entries (expensive) or rely on external GC manifests?
- encryption: optional envelope encryption metadata for payloads (KMS key id). Where to put that? ext TLV or separate store metadata?

Immediate todos (me):
- quick proto: implement minimal ser/de in rust with zero-dependency varint and crc32 (target 4 hrs).
- write unit tests for resync heuristics (2 hrs).
- sync with storage team about payload-dedup heuristics and current blob fingerprints (1x meeting).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- This format intentionally steers away from JSON-in-blobs because proto + varint is smaller for small ints and edge friendly.
- Keep file header tiny and ascii so that simple "startsWith" checks can detect file type.
- Avoid TTL in manifest; eviction should be coordinated via out-of-band GC manifests to reduce manifest churn.

Small ascii diagram (seek & append):
FILE: [HEADER][E1][E2][E3]...[E64][FOOTER_INDEX->offsets]  <-- append-only, periodic footer
EDGE READ: scan E1..E64, stop at truncation -> last-good=E63 -> request blobs for E63 payloads and resume

If you pick this up: please keep each entry <512 bytes if possible. Big payloads must be referenced, not inlined.

References / inspiration:
- Seastar log segment layout (append-only, checksums)
- content-addressed storage + small index patterns from prior runtime work

If I forget: sync with Lina on the fingerprint vs sha model before prototyping digest storage.

-- end --
